name: Latent Diffusion / Stable Diffusion 1.x–2.x
sections: §3.1 perceptual compression; §3.2 latent diffusion; §4.1/Fig.7 compression evaluation; official sd-vae-ft-mse Training/Evaluation; SD1.5 VAE config
architecture: KL-regularized convolutional perceptual autoencoder with adversarial/perceptual reconstruction; latent C=4, spatial f=8 in SD1.5 (1024→128²×4). Cross-attention U-Net diffusion. LDM also studies VQ and other compression factors; these are not all SD1.5 configurations.
lineage: vs SD1: SAME anchor. vs SDXL: DISTINCT because SDXL explicitly retrains its AE from scratch. SD2 is not evidence of a fresh encoder: official ft-EMA/ft-MSE describes decoder-only fine-tuning, and SDXL §2.4 identifies the SD2 decoder change. Exact identity of every SD2 release is not established by this family description.
code: stable_diffusion/pipeline_stable_diffusion_img2img.py: get_timesteps, prepare_latents, __call__; native image+strength, floor(N×strength), encode then scheduler noise; VAE scaling. SD1.5 DDIM identity remains the anchor.
memory: No primary 1024 batch-one peak/time found. SD1.5 ≈0.86B U-Net implies ≈1.72 GB BF16 parameters alone (2 bytes/parameter); CLIP, VAE, activations, CFG and allocator add memory. Native training was512, so1024 is an extrapolation, not equivalent native-resolution quality. Frozen runtime remains unmeasured.
evaluation: Fig.7 compares f=1,2,4,8,16,32, 5K samples,500K CelebA-HQ or2M ImageNet updates, A100 and DDIM step sweeps; f4/8 balances speed and quality. Official decoder-ft card: COCO2017-val5K at256, original PSNR23.4±3.8dB/SSIM.69/rFID4.99 versus ft-MSE24.5±3.7/.71/4.70. Its PSIM column is not our LPIPS assessor.
implication: Retain SD1.5; do not count SD2.1 as independent-encoder transfer. The relevant mechanism is encoder initialization, not decoder fine-tuning or changed text encoders.
limitations: Generation/reconstruction metrics do not evaluate watermark survival. Official SD2 metadata endpoint was inaccessible; no new SD2 revision or gate status is invented.

name: SDXL
sections: §2.1 architecture; §2.4 improved autoencoder; Table3 reconstruction; official VAE config and img2img prepare_latents
architecture: KL AutoencoderKL,C=4,f=8; same architecture class as SD1, separately trained. SDXL U-Net≈2.6B, dual CLIP conditioning; native1024. Optional refiner excluded from core.
lineage: vs SD1: YES, explicit from-scratch AE training in §2.4,batch256 versus9,EMA. vs SDXL: SELF anchor. Similar architecture does not imply weight ancestry.
code: stable_diffusion_xl/pipeline_stable_diffusion_xl_img2img.py: native image+strength and get_timesteps/prepare_latents. The frozen protocol executes the pinned official fp16 checkpoint values in full fp32 VAE arithmetic; it does not replace the artifact with the separate fp32 file or an external fp16-fix model.
memory: No matched primary batch-one1024 peak/time. The roughly2.6B U-Net implies at least5.2GB BF16 parameters plus dual CLIP and fp32 VAE execution/activations. Frozen stage2 selected SDXL assets total6.941187536GB. Earlier7.105319356GB estimate used a different selection and is superseded, not an amendment of the asset plan. Official fp16 VAE is167,335,342 bytes versus separate fp32 artifact334,643,268 bytes; file precision differs from execution precision. Core10–14h is a project estimate, not a primary measurement.
evaluation: Table3 COCO2017-val256: SDXL PSNR24.7/SSIM.73/LPIPS.88/rFID4.4; SD1 23.4/.69/.96/5.0; SD2 24.5/.71/.92/4.7. Preserve paper metric convention rather than treating these LPIPS values as the thesis assessor. Generation preferences can include refiner and cannot be assigned to base-only img2img.
implication: Retain R1 as the strongest documented independent-encoder anchor, with full fp32 VAE execution of the pinned official checkpoint and deterministic posterior-mode D1.
limitations: Reconstruction at256 does not predict1024 survival. From-scratch training is an author statement, not independent initialization forensics.

name: Stable Diffusion 3 / 3.5
sections: §3 rectified flow; §5.2.1/Table3 VAE channels; AppendixE.1/Table7 component memory/throughput
architecture: MMDiT rectified flow, KL VAE C=16/f=8 with latent scale/shift. SD3.5 grouped withSD3; model size/version is not a fresh AE family.
lineage: vs SD1: UNKNOWN initialization. vs SDXL: UNKNOWN initialization. Table3 proves a wider bottleneck and improved reconstruction, but does not explicitly establish random initialization or absence of SD weights.
code: stable_diffusion_3/pipeline_stable_diffusion_3_img2img.py: native image+strength; get_timesteps/encode with shift+scale and flow scheduler. Equal numeric DDIM/flow strength is not equal corruption.
memory: 2B denoiser≥4GB BF16 weights. AppendixE.1: VAE encoder weights.14GB and2.45ms forward at batch32; T5 weights19.05GB. Component reports are not1024 batch-one peak/runtime. Complete residentT5 pipeline needs offload/more memory; candidate runtime unknown.
evaluation: Table3 C16 VAE PSNR28.62/SSIM.86/FID1.06 versus C4 25.12/.75/2.41; dataset/resolution not clear in inspected caption, so do not assign COCO/1024. Generator-quality gains do not establish encoder-transfer survival.
implication: Potential larger-panel architecture contrast if access and ancestry gaps resolved; exclude gated models now.
limitations: SD3Medium noncommercial research terms; SD3.5 Community terms differ. Both API snapshots auto-gated. Public text does not authorize gated weights.

name: Kandinsky 2.x / MoVQ (3.x/5.x grouped)
sections: §4 components/MoVQ; §5 quantitative/human evaluation; MoVQ configs; KD2.2 encode/decode
architecture: Image-embedding prior, diffusion decoder and MoVQ,C=4/f=8. Kandinsky3 enlarges MoVQ; Kandinsky5 images use FLUX.1-dev VAE, so the brand is not a persistent encoder lineage.
lineage: vs SD1/SDXL: documented separate MoVQ training, qualified YES. Sber-trained MoVQ on LAION-HighRes67M is training evidence, not an inference from different names or datasets. Initialization is less explicit than SDXL.
code: Pinned v0.36.0 kandinsky2_2/pipeline_kandinsky2_2_img2img.py and models/autoencoders/vq_model.py: native image+strength; KD2.2 decode can bypass nearest-codebook quantization with force_not_quantize=True. Paper quantization ablations are not automatically the runtime path.
memory: KD2.2 decoder package≈5.284GB plus prior≈10.574GB on disk, not peakVRAM. KD3 components total28.391GB (text21.739,U-Net6.111,MoVQ.541); phased offload needed on24GB. Matched1024 peak/runtime unknown.
evaluation: §5 COCO30K256: linear-prior FID8.03; diffusion-prior quantized9.86 versus unquantized9.87. Human DrawBench5,000 votes. These are generation, not native1024 regeneration/watermark metrics.
implication: Highest-priority additional convolutional encoder: native strength API, permissive ungated packages, documented MoVQ training. AE-only diagnostic cheaper than full prior+decoder regeneration.
limitations: KD2.2 native resolution lower than1024; KD3 better1024 proposal. Fix quantization mode explicitly. Independence conclusion does not extend toKandinsky5.

name: SANA / DC-AE / SANA-Sprint
sections: §2 DC-AE/linearDiT/text; §4 benchmark protocol; Table5 latency/quantization; paired DC-AE/Sprint cards
architecture: DC-AE continuous nonvariational C32/f32 (1024→32²×32), residual shortcuts and linear-attention DiT, Gemma2-2B. Sprint is distilled, not another family.
lineage: vs SD1/SDXL: documented separate DC-AE training, qualified YES; no SD checkpoint initialization described. Compression geometry alone would not suffice; DC-AE §3 supplies training evidence.
code: sana/pipeline_sana.py T2I-only. sana/pipeline_sana_sprint_img2img.py exposes image+strength with TrigFlow time transform/default2steps; v0.36 also has Sprint img2img. floor(N×strength) can give zero steps for .1/.2/.4 at tinyN; core strengths cannot simply be copied.
memory: Table5 RTX4090 1024 FP16 .88s versus optimized W8A8 .37s, with quality changes. Official4bit8GB claim uses Nunchaku. These are optimizedT2I, not frozen img2img measurements. 600M denoiser≥1.2GB BF16 plus≈4GB Gemma/AE/activations; target runtime unknown.
evaluation: GenEval533 prompts as paper states, DPG1,065,MJHQ30K. Table5 quantization CLIP28.5→28.3 and ImageReward1.03→.96 on statedMJHQ/first1K subsets. DC-AE supplies reconstruction evidence; Sprint few-step gains do not validate equal corruption.
implication: DC-AE provides large compression change and cheap AE-only contrast. FullSprint needs a defensible corruption schedule and cannot silently replaceR1.
limitations: Apache ungated packages; upstreamGemma terms/access remain separate. Packaged weights do not erase upstream terms. Optimized headlines do not establish frozen-stack24GB throughput.

name: PixArt-α / PixArt-Σ
sections: §3.2 KV compression; §3.3 VAE adaptation; §4.1/4.2 evaluation; paired α methods/evaluation
architecture: 0.6B DiT/T5, KL VAE C4/f8. α uses pretrained LDM VAE; Σ explicitly replaces with SDXL VAE and adapts denoiser2K updates. α paper does not establish exactSD1.5 versusSD2 checkpoint.
lineage: α vs SD1: shared pretrainedLDM lineage, not proven new. Σ vs SD1: inherits SDXL distinct ancestry; Σ vs SDXL: SAME. No new encoder diversity.
code: pixart_alpha/pipeline_pixart_sigma.py T2I signature; no image/strength. Community adapter is not native support in inspected official class.
memory: Denoiser≥1.2GB BF16 plusT5/VAE. No matched1024 batch-one peak/seconds. ≈34% KV compression relative high-resolution speed improvement is not a portable absolute1024 measurement.
evaluation: Σ evaluates30K curated high-quality examples and300-caption human/GPT4V preference subset. α COCO30K FID7.32. α753 A100GPU-days partly converts V100 by2.2×; training estimate, not inference cost.
implication: Useful denoiser control holding SDXL encoder fixed, low priority for encoder diversity.
limitations: Ungated OpenRAIL++ packages, not Apache/MIT permissiveness. Private evaluation/evaluator differences prevent direct score ranking.

name: Playground v2.5
sections: §2 EDM/noise/resolution buckets; §3/Table1 MJHQ/preference; official VAE config/LFS metadata
architecture: SDXL-like U-Net with EDM and balanced resolution buckets; C4/f8 SDXL VAE.
lineage: vs SD1: inherits SDXL ancestry. vs SDXL: SAME. Advertised fp16VAE LFS SHA matches officialSDXL (bcb60880…c6161e68); metadata identity without downloading weights.
code: stable_diffusion_xl/pipeline_stable_diffusion_xl_img2img.py supports architecture; EDM scheduler/config compatibility remains a condition, not tested runtime.
memory: ≈2.6B denoiser≥5.2GB BF16 plustext/VAE/activations. No matched primary1024 peak/time. Similar parameter count does not justify copying latency across schedulers.
evaluation: MJHQ30K1024 FID4.48 versusSDXL+refiner9.55; private1K-prompt aesthetic preference4.8×ratio. Settings mix model/sampler/training differences, not AE isolation.
implication: Exclude from encoder-diversity expansion; at most a separate denoiser/scheduler control.
limitations: Custom Playground Community license, ungated. AdvertisedVAE hash is metadata evidence, not locally verified weights.

name: Hunyuan-DiT
sections: §2.1 VAE/text/DiT; §4 evaluation/ablations; official cards/config
architecture: ≈1.5B transformer with bilingualCLIP/T5; C4/f8 VAE explicitly fromSDXL.
lineage: vs SD1: inheritsSDXL ancestry. vs SDXL: SAME. Hunyuan text callsSDXL fine-tunedSD1.5, conflicting with creatorSDXL§2.4; prefer original from-scratch account and preserve conflict.
code: hunyuandit/pipeline_hunyuandit.py T2I-only, no source image/strength. HunyuanImage3 is separate80B-MoE generation; no inherited VAE-lineage assertion.
memory: 1.5B denoiser≥3GB BF16 plustext/VAE; matched1024 peak/time unknown. HunyuanImage3 advertised weights≈168GB; activeMoE parameters do not equal resident memory.
evaluation: §4 >3,000 prompts,>50 professional raters,four dimensions,30–50 prompts/subcategory. Smaller.7B ablations COCO30K256. Do not assign those conditions to1024 full-model reconstruction/survival.
implication: DiT adds no encoder diversity. Image3 remains current lead with unresolved AE ancestry and huge resident footprint.
limitations: Tencent custom terms, ungated hub; availability is not permissiveness. Native strength wrapper not verified.

name: Qwen-Image / newer Qwen variants
sections: §2.3 image VAE: frozen Wan encoder and decoder-only fine-tuning; Table2 reconstruction; architecture discussion and official configs/native img2img
architecture: 20B MMDiT/Qwen2.5VL, Wan2.1 VAE C16/spatial8/temporal4. Image encoder frozen, decoder fine-tuned. Qwen2.1 instead RGBA4 input/output,z64,spatial16/temporal8; no inheritedWan assumption.
lineage: Original vs SD1/SDXL: qualified distinctWan training lineage, not newly trainedQwen encoder. Qwen2.1 vsboth UNKNOWN. Qwen-VAE2 from-scratch ablations do not establish mapping to released2.1.
code: qwenimage/pipeline_qwenimage_img2img.py native image+strength, mean/std normalization/flow truncation. qwenimage21/pipeline_qwenimage21.py image conditioning but no strength; not interchangeable.
memory: The20B denoiser requires at least40GB BF16 parameters, plus about14GB for the7B text encoder, VAE and activations. A fully resident24GB pipeline is impossible under these assumptions. Offload/quantization changes runtime; no matched primary1024 peak/time found. Wan video8.19GB is not a Qwen1024 image measurement.
evaluation: Table2 ImageNet-val256FP32 PSNR33.42/SSIM.9159 versusWan31.29/.887; in-house text-rich25636.63/.9839 versus26.77/.9386. Effective image encoder19M/decoder25M. Decoder improvement does not prove new encoder.
implication: Wan/Qwen AE-only distinct-lineage diagnostic useful; fullregeneration costly. Treat2.1 as unresolved new config.
limitations: Qwen-Image/2512 are Apache and ungated. Qwen2.1 uses ungated Qwen Research terms, not Apache. The original paper cannot establish successor initialization.

name: Z-Image
sections: S3-DiT and distillation methods; §5.2.1/Table9; official speed claim and VAE metadata
architecture: 6B single-stream S3-DiT with Qwen3-4B conditioning; frozen FLUX1 VAE, C=16/f=8. Turbo uses 8 NFE.
lineage: Against SD1 and SDXL: UNKNOWN through FLUX initialization. The advertised VAE LFS SHA f5b59a26…604d40a3 matches FLUX1 and Chroma; this is encoder reuse, not new training.
code: z_image/pipeline_z_image_img2img.py native image+strength, VAEshift/scale/flow. Currentpin; frozen v0.35.1 compatibility not established.
memory: The 6B denoiser alone requires at least 12 GB BF16 weights, plus about 8 GB for the 4B text encoder and additional VAE/activations. Primary subsecond speed uses H800, FlashAttention3 and compilation. The modelcard 16 GB claim does not prove a fully resident BF16 pipeline. Our 1024 peak and runtime remain unknown.
evaluation: Table9 reports GenEval .84 for base and .82 for Turbo. Speed depends on NFE and specialized optimization; quality scores do not isolate the encoder. Prompt rewriting and distillation can affect outcomes.
implication: An accessible modern FLUX-family contrast, but not a proven freshly initialized AE. Replacing gated FLUX with Z-Image would not establish independent-encoder transfer.
limitations: Apache2 and ungated model package. Published object hashes are metadata evidence; no weights or outcomes were generated.

name: Lumina-Image 2.0
sections: UnifiedNextDiT architecture; official README VAE statement; §5.4/Table8; Fig11 efficiency protocol
architecture: 2.6B UnifiedNextDiT with Gemma2-2B and FLUX VAE, C=16/f=8. Progressive multiresolution training, RoPE and CFG normalization improve the denoiser.
lineage: Against SD1 and SDXL: UNKNOWN through FLUX. The VAE is reused, not separately trained for Lumina.
code: lumina2/pipeline_lumina2.py: T2I only, default 30 steps, no image/strength parameter.
memory: Denoiser weights alone are at least 5.2 GB BF16, plus about 4 GB Gemma and VAE/activations. Fig11 compares A100 batch-one 1024 latency graphically; exact seconds were not reliably extracted. Target-device peak/runtime remain unknown.
evaluation: Table8: low-resolution DPG84.5/GenEval.63 → high-resolution85.7/.67 → high-quality5K updates87.2/.73 →11K updates87.6/.72. Nonmonotonic GenEval requires retaining training-stage context. FDPM/TeaCache speed choices trade stability or blur.
implication: A further FLUX reuse example, low priority for an independent-encoder panel.
limitations: Apache ungated package; upstream Gemma license/access remain separate dependencies. No native strength interface is assumed.

name: HiDream-I1 / O1 successor (one conservative family)
sections: MoE/training methods; benchmark tables; official README lines105/109 and VAE config; paired O1 methods/evaluation
architecture: I1 uses a 17B sparse-MoE DiT, four text encoders and FLUX1 VAE, C=16/f=8. O1 is native RGB3/f1 unified pixel diffusion; its separate card is conservatively grouped under this one family.
lineage: I1 ancestry against SD1/SDXL is UNKNOWN through FLUX. README names FLUX.1-schnell while config _name_or_path is ../checkpoints/flux-dev: both support FLUX1 family reuse, not byte identity. O1 has no AE, so encoder independence is not applicable. Qwen3-VL denoiser initialization is not AE initialization.
code: hidream_image/pipeline_hidream_image.py is I1 T2I only. O1 custom inference.py accepts reference images for editing/subject conditioning, but is not native Diffusers strength-controlled img2img; see its separate card.
memory: I1 denoiser alone requires at least34GB BF16 before T5/Llama8B/CLIP/VAE. O1 index reports8,804,887,792 parameters:17.609775584GB BF16 parameter floor, excluding activations/KV. Eight official files total35.219643552GB on disk. Added to20.206GB core gives55.425643552GB before packages/images, below the future authorized80GB cap but not an execution authorization. Target1024 peak/runtime unknown; current O1 interface snaps square requests to2048.
evaluation: I1 reports GenEval .83, DPG85.89 and HPSv2.1 mean33.82. Paper 50/28/14-step variants differ from the native Fast16 example; preserve revisions. Sample count/resolution are incomplete in the table. O1 GenEval .90 and DPG89.83 support pixel generation potential, not corruption equivalence.
implication: I1 adds no encoder lineage. O1 leads a high-resolution pixel-method research proposal because methods/evaluations are substantive; PRX remains the more direct native1024 interface candidate. Neither is ready for the frozen strength-controlled experiment.
limitations: MIT ungated model packages. I1 external Llama3.1 is gated. O1 optional Gemma prompt refiner is gated; plain inference loads the local bundled model/processor, not a required external text encoder. No runtime validation.

name: OmniGen v1
sections: §2/3 architecture/training; Table2 and editing evaluation; official docs/inference.md memory/time table
architecture: 3.8B Phi3-initialized multimodal rectified flow with frozen SDXL VAE, C=4/f=8. Input images are instruction/context tokens, not necessarily source latents initialized with partial noise.
lineage: Against SD1: inherits SDXL separately trained ancestry. Against SDXL: SAME frozen encoder.
code: omnigen/pipeline_omnigen.py accepts input_images and img_guidance_scale, but no strength. Native editing is not demonstrated SDEdit.
memory: Official repo d4752019ae16741dc3801fd4989432aad4c81a4f reports1024: A800 text9GB31s/single image12GB66s/two images13GB80s; RTX3090 text9GB77s/single12GB166s/two13GB203s. KV caching/offload and separate CFG are enabled, model offload false. With model offload,3090 single image5GB469s. Precision/steps are incompletely specified; these are author reports, not our measurements.
evaluation: Table2 GenEval overall .70 versus SD3 .68; task tests include EmuEdit and DreamBench. Editing capability does not validate matched-strength regeneration. Resource measurements show an offload latency tradeoff.
implication: No encoder diversity. It demonstrates why fitting 24 GB and fitting 15 hours are different constraints.
limitations: MIT ungated model. Resource table uses official custom code; current Diffusers may differ, so reported seconds cannot be transferred blindly.

name: Würstchen / Stable Cascade
sections: §3 three-stage compression; §4.1 COCO/PickScore; §4.2/Table2; Fig4; successor modelcard
architecture: Stage A VQ reconstruction uses spatial f=4; Stage B reconstructs its latent; Stage C uses a semantic EfficientNetV2-S compressor with16 channels and about24×24 tokens for1024, effective f≈42.7. This is not a single f8 VAE. Stable Cascade successor sizes differ from the paper.
lineage: Against SD1/SDXL: qualified YES for a distinct documented semantic compressor, ImageNet pretraining and stage training. This does not prove disjoint training data.
code: stable_cascade/pipeline_stable_cascade_prior.py allows images to condition the prior, but no strength. It does not expose source-latent partial denoising.
memory: Paper Fig4 A1001024 shows more than2× SDXL relative speed; exact portable peak/seconds unavailable. Stable Cascade3.6B prior alone requires at least7.2GB BF16 plus decoder/text/VQ. Sequential offload changes time; matched release1024 runtime unknown.
evaluation: COCO30K generated at1024, downsampled to256 for FID. Table2 Würstchen FID23.6/IS40.9; Stage C60 steps, Stage B12 steps, CFG4. PickScore also uses LocalNarratives5K and PartiPrompts. These are not measurements of the Stable Cascade3.6B release.
implication: A distinct semantic compression route, but noncommercial terms and non-equivalent conditioning reduce immediate feasibility.
limitations: Ungated custom noncommercial model license. Successor weights and stages prevent direct reuse of paper timing or scores.

name: Pixel-space DDPM
sections: §3 forward/reverse process and objective; §4/Table1; AppendixB architecture and sampling cost
architecture: RGB C=3/f=1, no AE. U-Net predicts noise with group normalization and attention at16². Training uses1000 steps and beta1e-4→.02.
lineage: Against SD1 and SDXL: NOT APPLICABLE, no AE. This tests regeneration without an AE bottleneck, not another independently trained encoder.
code: ddpm/pipeline_ddpm.py accepts batch_size and num_inference_steps, not image/strength. Pixel SDEdit requires forward-noising and correct scheduler truncation; not implemented or authorized.
memory: The114M model requires at least .228GB BF16 parameters. Paper sampling on TPUv3-8 takes300s for batch128 at256; not GPU batch-one or1024. Official face checkpoint supports256; no validated1024 setting, peak or latency.
evaluation: Table1 CIFAR train-reference FID3.17 (test-reference5.24), IS9.46. LSUNChurch256 FID7.89 and Bedroom4.90. These unconditional domain metrics do not validate general-photo regeneration.
implication: Feasible permissive ungated small mechanism control, but demoted from the lead pixel proposal because high-resolution pixel alternatives exist. It cannot stand in for general-photo1024 regeneration.
limitations: Apache2 model and permissive diffusion code. An adapter would be new scientific work;256 feasibility does not establish1024 feasibility.

name: Microsoft Lens
sections: §2.2 FLUX2 VAE and architecture; §2.5 acceleration; §3/Table2 and protocols; official README
architecture: 3.8B48-block MMDiT with frozen FLUX2 VAE, C=32/f=8;2×2 packing gives128 channels/f16 token grid. GPT-OSS20B total/about3B active text encoder.
lineage: Against SD1/SDXL: UNKNOWN through FLUX2 initialization. Explicit reuse means a freshly trained Lens denoiser is not a fresh AE.
code: Official microsoft/Lens repo5bf0f0cea2f4bc32ebb2b7ed2ef96d5e88b701e0 has a custom pipeline. No Lens native Diffusers class in inspected tree, nor verified source-noise image+strength interface.
memory: §2.5 reports1024 on H100:20 steps3.15s and4-step Turbo.84s. Denoiser floor7.6GB BF16; dequantized GPT-OSS20B on A100 adds about40GB, unlike Hopper MXFP4. Target peak/runtime unknown; reasoner cost is not assumed included.
evaluation: Table2: Lens20-step GenEval.930 and Turbo4-step.914; OneIG EN/ZH are separate columns (.557/.525 for Lens), not two GenEval settings. Protocols include OneIG1,120 prompts, GenEval553 as this paper states and LongText160. Default inference refines prompts with a reasoner, uses20 steps/CFG5, while Turbo4-step uses no CFG. Prompt rewriting and system-prompt search therefore limit comparison with frozen unrewritten prompts. The H100 .84s/3.15s speed reports are primary author measurements, not our replication.
implication: Current efficiency lead but no new encoder lineage. Advertised model API401 and empty owner search mean access unavailable, not proof of nonexistence.
limitations: Code MIT. Actual model revision/license unverified at inaccessible endpoint. GPU-specific quantization undermines a blanket small-VRAM claim.

name: PixelGen
sections: §3.1–3.4 pixel prediction/perceptual losses; ImageNet/T2I evaluations; official PixelAE/config/actual sampler
architecture: RGB C=3/f=1 with affine identity PixelAE: encode x/scale+shift, inverse decode. Clean-image prediction converts to flow. LPIPS, perceptual DINO and REPA losses train the model; no compression AE.
lineage: Against SD1/SDXL: NOT APPLICABLE, no AE. Training perceptual networks are not inference compressors.
code: Official repo7b94115d6f14d1c4ce0fe7a17a06351934ef2d4a: T2I config uses adam_sampling.AdamLMSamplerJiT and PixelAE. Sampler starts from noise; no verified image+strength adapter. Generic sampling.py is not the configured sampler. No official native Diffusers support verified.
memory: ImageNet676M model floor1.352GB BF16; T2I1.1B floor2.2GB plus text/activations. Native T2I512; no1024 peak/time. Token/attention scaling is not captured by parameter memory.
evaluation: ImageNet256,80 epochs without CFG: FID5.11;160 epochs with CFG and50 Heun steps: FID1.83. T2I5121.1B GenEval.79. Paper title “Pixel Diffusion Beats Latent Diffusion with Perceptual Loss” differs from repository “Improving Pixel Diffusion with Perceptual Loss”; retain version distinction.
implication: Modern pixel-method evidence and lower model size, but native512 and code-license gap put it behind HiDream-O1 for P7.
limitations: Official HF weights Apache2 and ungated. Repository tree lacks LICENSE; do not infer code permission from weight terms. Community Diffusers mirror is not official support.

name: PixSGR
sections: §3.1 low-channel bottleneck; §3.2 sparse global refinement; ImageNet protocol/tables; official release inventory
architecture: Pixel diffusion with learned low-channel bottleneck and sparse global refinement inside the denoiser. RGB3/f1 output, no external pretrained AE.
lineage: Against SD1/SDXL: NOT APPLICABLE. Internal representation learning can still remove marks; pixel space does not guarantee retention.
code: CVL-UESTC/PixSGR repo1f08f332fb469c893cfa8992ad269d8588173c5a exposes README/assets, no runnable sampler inspected. HF contains only .gitattributes and no released weights. Native Diffusers support unverified.
memory: 875M parameters imply at least1.75GB BF16 weights. Evaluation at256/512; no supported1024 model or primary1024 peak/time. Availability gap blocks an executable cost plan.
evaluation: ImageNet256,50K samples,320 epochs,875M model: FID1.51, IS311, precision.78, recall.65. CFG3 over[.2,.98], interval guidance.04 over[.2,.7]. These are evaluation settings, not .2 img2img strength. No general T2I1024 result established.
implication: Qualifies as substantively inspected distinct research, not an executable candidate. Paper evidence and released-model availability are separate.
limitations: Ungated but empty HF repository; license/code/weights unavailable rather than gated.

name: DC-AE supporting encoder evidence
sections: §3 residual shortcuts/three-phase training; reconstruction tables; high-resolution efficiency comparisons
architecture: Continuous nonvariational deep-compression AE; SANA uses C32/f32. Paper studies f64/c128 and f128/c512 too; denoiser patch size is separate from AE compression.
lineage: Against SD1/SDXL: qualified distinct training lineage. Three phases train on ImageNet/SAM/Mapillary/FFHQ; no SD initialization is stated. Architectural resemblance alone is not independence evidence.
code: DC-AE encode/decode is used by Sana and Sprint classes. Standalone reconstruction is possible conceptually, but no execution/adapter was built.
memory: Primary19.1× H100 speedup concerns UViT-H512, not1024 batch-one AE or full-generation latency. AE-only memory/seconds unknown; dense weights and activations must be measured later.
evaluation: Table2 ImageNet512 reconstruction: f64/c128 rFID16.84→.22 and f128/c512100.74→.23 with the proposed training/shortcuts. Reconstruction tradeoffs do not imply better preservation of a watermark.
implication: Supports the SANA family independence rationale; does not add another family to the floor.
limitations: No full diffusion result can be inferred from encoder-only reconstruction quality.

name: SANA-Sprint supporting distillation evidence
sections: §3 flow-to-TrigFlow/self-consistency/adversarial distillation; §4.1/4.2 benchmarks and latency
architecture: Same DC-AE C32/f32; SANA denoiser distilled to1–4 steps. Conversion rescales time, SNR and model output between flow matching and TrigFlow.
lineage: Same DC-AE encoder as SANA, not an additional independently trained AE. Against SD1/SDXL use the qualified training evidence in dcae.md.
code: sana/pipeline_sana_sprint_img2img.py exposes image+strength, default2 steps, TrigFlow-specific time bounds. Small-step integer truncation can empty the core .1/.2/.4 schedule.
memory: Headline1024 one-step .1s H100/.31s RTX4090 uses optimized conditions. Another table gives .21s for600M one-step and .32s four-step: different configurations must not be merged. Our img2img time/peak unknown;1.6B denoiser BF16 floor3.2GB plus text/AE.
evaluation: MJHQ30K FID/CLIP and GenEval comparisons: headline one-step FID7.59/GenEval.74; four-step table FID6.48/GenEval.76. Faster sampling is not evidence of matched source corruption.
implication: Cheap generation candidate after a separate schedule design, or DC-AE-only diagnostic now as a proposal. No silent schedule amendment.
limitations: Distilled speed claims do not justify assuming strength labels have the same meaning as DDIM.

name: Wan supporting Qwen encoder lineage
sections: §4.1.1/4.1.2 causal VAE and training; Fig7 reconstruction/throughput; §4.7.1 WanBench
architecture: 127M causal3D VAE, C16/spatial8/temporal4; first image frame only undergoes spatial compression. Train2D image AE then inflate to3D with L1/KL/LPIPS followed by adversarial learning.
lineage: Qualified separate documented training vs SD1/SDXL; initial2D checkpoint random initialization is not explicit. Qwen freezes this encoder and fine-tunes decoder; not a second new encoder.
code: Original Qwen img2img is an image-specific consumer of the Wan-derived AE; no claim that video pipelines implement a matched1024 image attack.
memory: Video8.19GB report belongs to video settings. Fig7 uses720²25-frame reconstruction/throughput, not1024 image batch-one peak/time. Standalone image AE runtime unknown.
evaluation: WanBench1,035 cases/model and VBench14B86.22%; video evaluation is not image regeneration. Fig7 numerical image values were not reliably extracted, so no fabricated PSNR/latency is listed.
implication: Training lineage supports a Qwen/Wan AE-only proposal with a different bottleneck and decoder history.
limitations: Counted under Qwen family for the conservative floor, not as an extra family just for AE reuse.

name: Kandinsky3 MoVQ detail
sections: §3.4/Table2 MoVQ sizes/training; evaluation; updated2410.21061 §4 architecture and human protocol
architecture: C4/f8 MoVQ; compares67M,102M,270M and selects270M. Updated model combines roughly3B U-Net and8.6B FLAN-UL2 text encoder.
lineage: Against SD1/SDXL: qualified separate MoVQ training on LAION-HighRes. No fresh family count beyond Kandinsky2/3 grouping. AE is frozen during generator training.
code: v0.36.0 kandinsky3/pipeline_kandinsky3_img2img.py provides image+strength; official native1024 model. Quantization path must be fixed from source, not assumed from the term MoVQ.
memory: Advertised component bytes: text21.739GB, U-Net6.111GB, MoVQ.541GB, total28.391GB. These are disk/weight amounts, not peak; phase offload needed24GB. Primary matched1024 time/peak unknown.
evaluation: Table2 ImageNet reconstruction270M FID.686/SSIM.741/PSNR27.04, latent32². Do not invent an image resolution absent from the inspected table caption. Updated report uses human comparisons; these are not watermark outcomes.
implication: Best optional full1024 regenerator among documented independent MoVQ variants, subject to timing and explicit proposal approval.
limitations: A larger MoVQ model is not automatically independent of earlier MoVQ training; count the family once.

name: Kandinsky5 image lineage correction
sections: §5.1–5.3 CrossDiT/encoders; §8.2.8 image-generation/editing SBS; official current Diffusers I2I signature
architecture: Image Lite6B CrossDiT flow matching; explicitly FLUX.1-dev VAE C16/f8. Video uses HunyuanVideo VAE. The image branch is not MoVQ.
lineage: Against SD1/SDXL: UNKNOWN through FLUX1. Does not inherit Kandinsky2/3 distinct MoVQ encoder lineage.
code: kandinsky5/pipeline_kandinsky_i2i.py accepts image and prompt, default50 steps/CFG3.5, but no strength. Native instruction editing is not the frozen source-noise attack.
memory: 6B image denoiser floor12GB BF16 plus Qwen2.5VL7B text conditioning/VAE. No matched primary1024 image peak/time; video acceleration figures cannot be reused.
evaluation: §8.2.8 uses internal SBS prompts expanded from PartiPrompts with GigaMax; expert judges rate prompt following/visual quality against FLUX-dev/Qwen and editing counterparts. Figure win percentages and exact sample count were not extracted; remain unknown. Video2.7× speedup is not image timing.

limitations: Paper inspected V2, but exact image checkpoint revision/license/gate not resolved in this sweep. Treat those model-release fields unavailable, not inferred from old Apache Kandinsky.

name: Qwen-VAE2 supporting newer AE research
sections: §2 global shortcut/semantic alignment; §3 training; §6.1.1/6.1.3 reconstruction and SiT evaluations
architecture: Global space-to-channel shortcut plus semantic DINO alignment; studies f16/c64 and f16/c128 image AEs. These are not automatically the released Qwen2.1 RGBA z64/f16 checkpoint.
lineage: Paper includes from-scratch f16/c64 ablation. Independence of that experiment is evidence; mapping it to the newer released model remains UNKNOWN.
code: qwenimage21/pipeline_qwenimage21.py is conditional generation/editing without strength. No verified released checkpoint mapping to the paper AE configurations.
memory: No matched1024 peak/time. Higher latent channel count does not alone determine peak memory; DINO loss is a training component, not necessarily inference residency.
evaluation: ImageNet256 and FFHQ1024 reconstruction; OmniDoc roughly3K images at256, f16/c128 PSNR30.45/SSIM.9706/NED.9617 versus FLUX1 NED.9546. SiT80-epoch no-CFG comparisons change patch rates. NED convention and OCR quality matter; not our mark detector.
implication: Potential additional encoder lineage for future work, conditional on exact release provenance; no automatic independent status for Qwen2.1.
limitations: Supplement only, not an additional model family in the floor.

name: HiDream-O1 native pixel model and P7 recommendation
sections: §3.2–3.4 unified pixel transformer/losses; §4 progressive training; §5 distillation/evaluation; official inference/pipeline/utils/index
architecture: Raw RGB C3/f1, no external VAE or disjoint text encoder; single shared text/image token system. Pixel patches32×32 are tokenization, not a learned AE compression. Qwen3-VL-8B initialization, clean-image prediction, LPIPS/perceptualDINO and flow conversion; distillation uses distribution matching/adversarial training.
lineage: Against SD1/SDXL: NOT APPLICABLE, no AE. The integrated vision tower for reference conditioning is not a source-image latent bottleneck for target generation.
code: Official repo2c2d29ff729e48f33e41f49edfdbd81d5ac103b4: inference.py loads local model_path processor/model in BF16 CUDA. generate_image(ref_image_paths,height,width,steps,...) has no strength; target initializes Gaussian RGB noise, references provide context. Full50 steps/CFG5/shift3; Dev28 steps/CFG0/shift1, flow_match editing versus flash elsewhere. No native Diffusers O1 class verified.
memory: Official index:8,804,887,792 parameters →17.609775584GB BF16 weight floor, excluding KV/activations/reference tokens. Tensor metadata35.219551168GB; eight files35.219643552GB. With20.206GB core,55.425643552GB before packages/images, below future80GB cap but not authorized now. No primary1024 peak/time. Crucially utils PREDEFINED_RESOLUTIONS includes2048² and~4MP rectangles, not1024; requested1024² snaps to2048². keep_original_aspect rescales toward2048² area, not a1024 bypass.
evaluation: §5/table1 8B GenEval.90, Pro.92; DPG8B89.83. Full50/Dev28-step protocols and multiple text/editing benchmarks provide substantive evaluation. Sampling resolution/sample counts are not fully specified for every table; leaderboard images are not independent measurements.
implication: P7: replace DDPM as lead high-resolution pixel research direction with O1, but retain PRX as the direct1024-interface lead. O1 is NOT a drop-in frozen1024 regenerator: no strength, resolution snapping, runtime unmeasured and new dependency stack. Any1024 adaptation or native instruction-editing scenario needs explicit proposal/design approval and separate interpretation.
limitations: MIT code/models, HF ungated. Plain inference uses bundled local weights/tokenizer/processor; optional Gemma4-31B prompt agent requires gate acceptance, optional API can cost money. Neither optional reasoner is required for plain generation or authorized here. PyTorch≥2.10/Transformers4.57.1 and optional FlashAttention differ from frozen stack.

name: FLUX1, FLUX2 and FLUX3 native model evidence
sections: Official modelcards Architecture/Usage/Limitations; official autoencoder code; current model API gates; FLUX2 Klein pipeline signature
architecture: FLUX1 C16/f8,12B flow transformer. FLUX2 C32/f8 with2×2 packing gives128 channels/f16 token grid; code ch_mult=[1,2,4,4]. FLUX3 is a newer flow-map release, not proof of newly initialized AE.
lineage: Against SD1/SDXL: UNKNOWN initialization for all inspected FLUX generations. Different channels or names do not prove independent training. FLUX2 adoption by Lens is reuse.
code: v0.36.0 flux/pipeline_flux_img2img.py supports image+strength for FLUX1. Current flux2/pipeline_flux2_klein.py accepts image conditioning but no strength, despite being an editing pipeline.
memory: FLUX1 denoiser12B≥24GB BF16 before T5/VAE. FLUX2 Klein4B card claims~13GB/subsecond without matched conditions;9B~29GB. FLUX3 card reports B2001024 with prompt upsampler off: BF16 peak31GB,FP8 26GB,NVFP4 25GB; upsampler adds28GB on80GB devices. None measures our target1024 img2img.
evaluation: Native cards/code substantiate architectures and reported operational numbers, but no opened full FLUX training/evaluation paper establishes AE initialization or watermark behavior. Distinguish primary model evidence from paper V2; excluded from conservative18-paper floor.
implication: Retain gated FLUX1 exclusion. Ungated Klein4B is available under Apache but is not an equivalent strength-controlled replacement and not proven independently initialized.
limitations: API auto-gated: FLUX1-schnell despite Apache, FLUX1-dev customNC, FLUX2-dev/custom, Klein9B/custom, FLUX3/KommUnity. Klein4B ungated Apache. Public README availability is not ungated weight access.

name: DeepFloyd IF native primary model evidence
sections: Official IF modelcard architecture/training/evaluation/usage; IF repository resource notes; native img2img source
architecture: Three pixel diffusion stages64→256→1024, T5 text encoder, no AE in IF stages. Common example substitutes SDx4 latent upscaler for stage3, so that example is not fully pixel-space.
lineage: Against SD1/SDXL: no AE in true IF stages; substituted SD upscaler changes that conclusion.
code: deepfloyd_if/pipeline_if_img2img.py accepts image+strength, adds pixel noise. StageI operates64, then cascades; not a single native1024 source-preserving denoiser.
memory: Modelcard CPU-offload14GB and repo16GB stages1/2,24GB mixed full pipeline reports use different configurations. StageI4.3B floor8.6GB BF16 plus T5/superresolution. Matched fully pixel1024 img2img time/peak unknown.
evaluation: Primary card reports COCO30K FID6.66, StageI2.42M training steps at64 and1000-step cosine noise schedule. No paper V2 claim; native card is substantively inspected but not counted among18 paper families.
implication: Pixel mechanism example with native img2img, but gate/noncommercial terms and low-resolution cascade weaken feasibility.
limitations: Auto-gated custom DeepFloyd research license, not permissive/ungated. Do not describe substituted SD upscaler example as no-AE.

architecture: HD8.9B derived from FLUX1-schnell, VAE C16/f8 with same advertised FLUX object. Radiance card is a short WIP pixel-model announcement; architecture was not sufficiently documented to assert an exact bottleneck.

name: PRX Pixel native1024 candidate
sections: Official modelcard architecture/usage; native prx pipeline signature and pixel noise path
